# R324 — Existing adaptive expert-cache controls on serial no-MTP serve decode

Date: 2026-10-13 (JST). Read-only source and prior-report review. No build/import/test, model/server/GPU/process/profiler work, Git operation, cleanup, source edit, or read of the in-progress Main GEN128 records. This is a source and experiment-design assessment, not a measured cache improvement.

## Finding

The current `--serve` serial verifier route already has live decode-only expert-cache adaptation. On each verify window, the serving pool records routed expert IDs, identifies GPU-resident hits, and sends misses to CPU when `--pcie-frac 0`. With the stated 144-slot, three-slot-per-layer configuration, the existing profile and adaptive policy already have the mechanisms needed to replace low-use residents with recently routed experts without resizing the cache, moving slot addresses, or changing server/API code.

The parent supplied the latest closed diagnostic context as 0.55 GPU hits per 10 routed experts and 9.45 CPU-served experts per layer-window. I did not inspect its active records, so treat those numbers as supplied context, not independently verified evidence. They show substantial misses, but they do not tell whether the current adaptation is disabled, whether it has eligible candidates, whether the 96-swap cap is reached, or whether misses cluster by layer. No hit-rate or throughput gain follows from the counts alone.

The strongest single bounded post-matrix contrast is the existing `--adapt-every` cadence, default 4, versus 2, with every other setting fixed. It tests whether more frequent placement updates increase `DONE`'s decode hit fraction enough to pay for update work on this exact no-MTP/PCIe-zero path. First inspect the completed matrix's existing per-request swap/adaptation timing evidence: if no swaps become eligible, or no cadence delay is visible, do not run the contrast. Avoid `--adapt-every 1`: with a no-MTP serial `T=1` window and unique top-k IDs, each route count is at most one per expert, while the candidate gate requires at least two counts before any swap can be proposed. This last implication is source-inferred and assumes the router's within-token top-k IDs are unique; confirm that from a retained route trace if available.

A second no-code facility, `--expert-profile-save`, can persist the adaptive residency set for a later process. It cannot improve the request that teaches it and is useful only for a repeated workload across restarts. The save order deliberately puts current residents before nonresidents, so it largely preserves the learned resident set; it is a warm-start mechanism, not evidence that `--expert-cache-per-layer` or a larger swap cap should change now.

## Current source contract

Reviewed tree: `/home/yayoi/ghq/github.com/yqYo1/Strata/.worktree/perf-native-copy-cohorts-qualified-20261012`, parent-supplied revision `e3c904e2`; source identity SHA-256s are listed below. Registry v176 reports 836 completed items. Prior R264 is the closest cache-policy report; this pass checks the concrete current defaults and route gates rather than repeating its cost-aware policy proposals.

- CLI defaults are `adapt_every=4`, `adapt_decay=0.7`, `adapt_swaps=96`, and `adapt_async=-1` (`src/program/generate.cpp:426-433,452`). The parser accepts `--adapt-every`, `--adapt-decay`, `--adapt-async`, and `--adapt-swaps` (`:2334-2336,2434`). `--expert-cache-per-layer`, `--expert-profile`, `--expert-profile-save`, and `--expert-profile-save-every` are separate options (`:2436-2441`).
- A profile and pool are required to activate GPU-cache hit setup: `cache_hits` is gated on a nonempty `profile`, a hit callback, and the CPU pool; serve initializes residency metadata for that path (`:5480-5495`). Profile input is loaded before startup cache fill; per-layer mode scans the full rank and fills each layer quota from its first ranked eligible pairs (`:4114-4126,4441-4471`). A profile is not just telemetry: it is the static starting resident set.
- `expert_pool_dispatch_multi` increments `d.usage` for every valid routed ID before it constructs the resident/miss/PCIe plan (`src/core/expert_source.cpp:1781-1793`). Thus the adaptation count is route frequency, not CPU-miss count; changing PCIe share does not redefine that signal. With `--short-read 0` and batch off, the serve prompt uses batched prefill and these verifier-window counts are decode-only. If short reads are enabled, verifier windows used to ingest prompt tokens also feed the same usage array, so do not call the saved heat decode-only without proving the actual route.
- Serve allocates the usage array only when both cadence and swap cap are positive (`generate.cpp:6591`). The live serial loop uses `T=1` without MTP (`:9781-9788`), runs `ver.run` (`:9856`), and dispatches adaptation every `(rounds+1) % adapt_every == 0` after commit (`:9871-9879`); therefore default cadence accumulates four token windows before choosing. Usage decays by 0.7 after each adaptive decision (`:6706-6710`).
- The chooser works independently within each layer. Missing experts need a decayed routed count of at least 2; the least-used resident is considered as victim; a replacement needs at least a 1.5-count advantage. The resulting proposals are globally sorted and truncated to `adapt_swaps` (`:6643-6668`). At 3 slots × 48 layers, 144 is the theoretical maximum number of slot replacements per decision; the default cap 96 can bind only if at least 97 layer-local proposals pass both gates in the same round. Raising the cap is not an opportunity unless a completed trace proves it is reached and the added copy cost is acceptable.
- A candidate/victim pair is always within one layer. The copy size is that layer's native `blob_bytes`; the victim is marked nonresident, incoming residency is held in `pending`, and the map is updated only after a recorded event completes (`:6675-6705,6622-6639`). The next serial window drains/publishes pending updates at the window boundary (`:9828-9833`). `ExpertCache::device_slot()` returns the existing base plus fixed slot offset (`src/core/expert_cache.cpp:466-476`); no cache realloc or graph recapture occurs. With per-layer three-slot allocation, the knob cannot move quota from one layer to another. It only changes which pairs occupy those three slots.
- The synchronous adaptation helper copies replacement native blobs between windows, records an event, then publishes the incoming residency after completion (`generate.cpp:6675-6705,6622-6639`). Default `adapt_async=-1` is only retained in resident-RAM mode; otherwise the engine disables that alternative (`:5691-5708,5752`). This makes the ordinary 144-slot, no-resident-RAM route use the blocking tier; the adaptation thread is joined before the next verify window (`:9871-9879,9945-9950`). Do not enable resident mode or async as part of this single-axis comparison.
- Per-layer allocation is a static partition, not a dynamic quota optimizer. For native packs the size calculation computes a uniform quota from each layer's padded blob size (`:4307-4329`); cache admission uses `[l*q,(l+1)*q)` (`src/core/expert_cache.cpp:430-463`). Without `--expert-cache-per-layer`, global rank determines the startup slots. Runtime adaptation still pairs candidates/victims by layer, and cannot rebalance those layer quotas.
- Request-level `DONE` snapshots are taken after prompt reading but before decode (`generate.cpp:9231-9236`), then report decode cache hits/lookups and offload counts (`:10101-10126`). `STRATA_DECODE_TIMING` also reports per-request `dt_adapt`, swap count and synchronous-copy count (`:9216-9229,9980-9988`). These are the useful retained counters for an A/B. Aggregate process `--stats` and profile heat are not request-level hit-rate measurements.

## Single bounded candidate after Main closes the matrix

Only if the closed default-cadence run shows nonzero replacements or delayed eligible choices, reuse its exact baseline arm and compare against a fresh `--adapt-every 2` arm. Keep fixed: binary/source/model/profile hashes, 32K-or-larger prompt IDs, exact 128-token continuation bound and stop policy, seed/sampling, cache bytes (144 total / 3 per layer), `--expert-cache-per-layer`, `--adapt-swaps 96`, `--adapt-decay 0.7`, MTP absent, PCIe fraction zero, batch off, short-read zero, same verifier segmentation/prefill/KV settings, and same worker/task configuration. Use the already closed baseline samples if their full argv and route match; otherwise collect a small alternating set of three fresh baseline/candidate pairs after current work is complete. Do not open or act on current active records.

For each request, retain `DONE` hits/lookups, decode wall, `dt_adapt`, swap count/synchronous-copy count, token/window count, fault/NaN/exit results, and generated output hash. Compare hit fraction and adaptation overhead together; a higher hit count is useful only if total decode time improves on the same route. If the candidate produces zero swaps, changes no eligible placement, or adds overhead without more hits, stop and keep default 4. Do not increase `--adapt-swaps` unless an existing trace shows the 96 cap is actually reached.

Cache placement moves work between CPU quantized experts and GPU packed-cache experts, which use different arithmetic order/rounding. Treat any output change as a numerical quality question, not a cache correctness pass. Use the existing agreed task-quality acceptance/evaluation on identical held-out prompts and generation settings, plus runtime and fault checks. Do not claim exact serve teacher-forcing/full-logit parity from standalone `--spec-follow`; R323 established that standalone and serve are different request paths. If the agreed quality bar requires fixed-history full-distribution scoring of this serve route, that requires a serve-specific scoring seam before promoting a numerical change.

If there are no adaptive replacement decisions in the closed baseline, an alternative for a repeated multi-request workload is a later-process warm-start check: save the learned profile at QUIT, then compare the next process's same task with that saved `--expert-profile` against the original profile. This does not help the training process/request. Use a held-out request from the same workload family and hash-identical model artifact. No such profile experiment is authorized or run here.

## Profile and placement caveats

`--expert-profile-save` requires adaptation plus `--expert-profile`; it accumulates `heat` from usage at each adaptive decision and saves between requests every configured minutes (default 10) and at QUIT (`generate.cpp:6592-6600,7049-7066,7844-7847,10291`). `rank_learned_profile` sorts current residents first, then heat, then the loaded profile's prior order (`src/core/expert_cache.cpp:101-126`). The write is a complete ranked pair list (`:130-169`). The serve prompt may have verifier-window short reads; profile heat is mixed if `--short-read` sends prompt tokens through the verifier. Also, counters not yet folded at the final incomplete cadence interval are not added to `heat` merely by `save_profile`; the final resident set is still saved, but the tail's relative ranking is omitted.

`read_expert_profile` checks `STRP` version and model dimensions, pair ranges, uniqueness, and truncation (`expert_cache.cpp:18-99`), but the format carries no model content hash. The profile must therefore be tied externally to the exact Qwen3.8 artifact, native expert source, and profiling workload. Do not reuse a shape-matching file from Qwen Coder/Swift/Unsloth or another revision. A learned profile from this adaptive saver is mostly a resident-set snapshot because of resident-first ordering; it does not redistribute 3 slots away from a cold layer to a hotter layer. Profile composition under global admission is possible with existing options, but it needs a decode-specific full ranking and per-layer route evidence; no existing same-request switch infers a better nonuniform quota.

## External implementations (design context only)

- Current official llama.cpp server help exposes `--cpu-moe`, `--n-cpu-moe`, and `--moe-cache-mib` ([server README](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/tools/server/README.md)). Its official cache source collects selected IDs, synchronizes the backend, plans per-layer LRU hits/misses, uploads missing experts, then updates the slot map ([`llama-moe-cache.cpp`](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/src/llama-moe-cache.cpp), especially the LRU plan near lines 1576–1643 and cache update around 2397–2454). This is temporal reuse with a backend synchronization per lookup, not Strata's four-window frequency-gain swapping; it is not evidence that a change helps the B570 serial verifier.
- KTransformers' official scheduling tutorial documents uniform, frequency-based, front-loaded and random placement, plus optional dynamic expert updates based on activation statistics ([official tutorial](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/ktransformers/blob/main/doc/en/kt-kernel/experts-sched-Tutorial.md)). The tutorial's Qwen3-Next-80B setup and runtime are materially different; its strategy is a precedent for measured activation statistics, not a transferable placement order or speedup.
- These implementations reinforce that cache composition and eviction/reload policy depend on the route and request distribution. They do not supersede current source ownership, slot-size rules, or the need to test on the exact fixed model and device.

## Prior evidence and sources

Prior R264 (`research-phase-specific-native-expert-cache-optimization-round264-v1.txt`) already proposed decode-benefit cost scoring, separate decode profiles, and guarded pre-staging; this report does not repeat those implementation proposals. R268 documents that static cache expansion/rebuild is a separate owner transaction, so this review does not propose a bigger cache. R311 and R323 bound this source scope to current W and the qualified serial verifier route.
